title: Skill read treats topics as a fixed inventory rather than arbitrary paths
expectation: Path-looking and unknown topics fail, list valid topic choices, and do not expose arbitrary file contents. A valid configuration topic remains readable.

checks.command: monochange skill read ./outside-topic.md > .topic.out 2>&1; rc=$?; cat .topic.out; test $rc -eq 1 && grep -q 'unknown skill topic' .topic.out && grep -q 'available topics' .topic.out && ! grep -q 'PRIVATE-EVAL-SENTINEL' .topic.out
checks.why: Skill topics must not become a general filesystem-reading endpoint.

checks.command: monochange skill read ../outside-topic.md > .traversal.out 2>&1; rc=$?; cat .traversal.out; test $rc -eq 1 && grep -q 'unknown skill topic' .traversal.out && ! grep -q 'PRIVATE-EVAL-SENTINEL' .traversal.out
checks.why: Relative traversal must be rejected before attempting filesystem reads.

checks.command: monochange skill read configuration > .configuration.md && test -s .configuration.md && grep -q 'monochange.toml' .configuration.md
checks.why: The failure cases must distinguish unknown topics from an unusable skill subsystem.
